content.text:
I submitted **index 19 (Bi 0.34, Fe 0.20, V 0.46)** as the best composition. At 31.4 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured. The submission was accepted but no score came back, so I don't know how it compares with the best composition in the library.

**Approach:** I only had 3 photocurrent measurements for 201 compositions, so I relied on prior knowledge rather than searching broadly. BiVO₄ is the strongest known light-absorbing electrode (photoanode) in the Bi-Fe-V system, so I looked only near a 1:1 Bi:V ratio with a little Fe. I spent the 5 XRD scans on candidates in that area. I then used the photocurrent measurements on the ones whose patterns showed a single BiVO₄-like crystal phase and no extra phases.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | XRD | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| **19** | 0.34 / 0.20 / 0.46 | single phase | **31.4 µA** |
| 14 | 0.39 / 0.17 / 0.44 | single phase | 23.9 µA |
| 81 | 0.35 / 0.23 / 0.42 | single phase | 16.2 µA |
| 85 | 0.39 / 0.20 / 0.41 | second phase present | not measured |
| 56 | 0.44 / 0.18 / 0.38 | several extra phases | not measured |

Within this small set, photocurrent fell as Fe went up (19 vs. 81) and as Bi went up (19 vs. 14). That suggests the true best may sit at somewhat higher V or lower Fe than index 19, for example indices 7, 23 or 24. I had no budget left to check them, so that remains untested.
